:::{#exm-specificity}
#### Specificity of a COVID-19 test

Suppose the COVID-19 test of @exm-sensitivity
is [negative](#def-negative-classification) for 99% of the people who do not have COVID-19.
Then its specificity (@def-specificity) is:

$$\Pr(\negclass \mid \neg D) = 0.99$$ {#eq-specificity-exm}

By the
[complement rule](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#cor-p-neg0)
and @thm-negative-classification-complement,
its false positive rate is:

$$
\ba
\Pr(\posclass \mid \neg D)
&= 1 - \Pr(\neg \posclass \mid \neg D)
&& \text{(complement rule, conditional on } \neg D \text{)} \\
&= 1 - \Pr(\negclass \mid \neg D)
&& \text{(negative classification is the complement of positive)} \\
&= 1 - 0.99
&& \text{(substitute the specificity)} \\
&= 0.01
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$ {#eq-specificity-exm-2}

:::
